memories.content: The rear entrance on the third floor of the Main Building connects directly to the pedestrian route leading to the Central Library.
With your back to the main entrance, Outdoor Parking Lot A is on the left.
With your back to the main entrance, the West Complex is on the left.
With your back to the main entrance, the Humanities Building is on the right.
The Student Centre is behind the Central Library.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is usually short.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route has a long indoor section.
The route from Outdoor Parking Lot C through the Student Centre accessible entrance to the west entrance of the Central Library does not pass through the Main Building.
In summer, students prefer the air-conditioned indoor route from the first to the third floor of the Main Building over the outdoor route.
Recommend only routes that are currently confirmed to be open.
Explain the distinction between the standard shortest route and the accessible route.
The route guidance agent can compare routes using stored geographic information.
The route guidance agent cannot check congestion in real time.
The route guidance agent cannot check for movable obstacles.
The route guidance agent cannot check in real time for newly installed temporary signs or movable control barriers at the time of inquiry.
There is no continuous accessible route that a wheelchair can use in the direction of the stairs on the right side of the Main Building.
The detour from the stairs on the right side of the Main Building to the Student Centre is long.
Mobility support companions prefer the indoor route through the Main Building to the Central Library because it is less affected by weather.
The public campus map shows building entrances and pedestrian paths between buildings.
The public campus map separately marks step-free accessible routes.
The pedestrian path in front of the Main Building's main entrance has a sign indicating the direction of the accessible route.
A step-free pedestrian path runs from Outdoor Parking Lot C to the Student Centre accessible entrance.
An accessible route runs from the Student Centre to the west entrance of the Central Library.
There is an above-ground pedestrian path from the West Complex to the Main Building's main entrance.
The pedestrian path from the Humanities Building to the Main Building's main entrance passes in front of the stairs on the right side of the Main Building.
Using the elevator from the first-floor lobby of the Main Building provides step-free access to the level of the third-floor rear entrance.
The escalator route in the Main Building includes a section where stairs cannot be avoided.
When step-free travel is required, direct people to the elevator route rather than the escalator route.
The elevator closest to the Main Building's main entrance is inside the first-floor lobby.
The above-ground route between the Main Building and the Central Library has a rest bench midway.
Solbit Plaza is between the Main Building's main entrance and the West Complex.
When it rains or snows, travel time on sloped outdoor pedestrian paths may be longer than usual.
Snow removal personnel judge that when it snows, major accessible routes must be cleared before other pedestrian paths.
Students going to the library after parking prefer the familiar, short Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route.
During class change times, pedestrian traffic increases between the third floor of the Main Building and the Central Library.
First-time visitors find directions based on visible facilities easier to understand than directions based on building numbers.
Because of the sloped terrain, first-time visitors sometimes confuse the levels of the Main Building's first-floor main entrance and third-floor rear entrance.
Delivery drivers consider designated service routes that do not mix with pedestrians more predictable and safer.
The route guidance agent cannot check on-site congestion in real time and can compare posted detours to identify routes with fewer branches.
The route guidance agent can distinguish stair routes from elevator routes on the public map.
The route guidance agent cannot measure on-site pedestrian traffic at the time of inquiry.
The route guidance agent cannot guarantee an individual user's travel time.
Check the current notice for the destination entrance before giving directions.
Do not recommend staff-only passages as detours to general users.
If the shortest route has stairs, also present an available accessible route.
In an emergency, instruct people to follow on-site evacuation signs and safety personnel's directions rather than general wayfinding guidance.
A pedestrian path from the West Gate stop to the Main Building's main entrance runs through Solbit Plaza.
There is a step-free route from the shuttle stop in front of the Student Centre to the west entrance of the Central Library.
Bicycle users dismount at the designated rack on the edge of Solbit Plaza and proceed on foot.
Do not suggest informal shortcuts that are not on the public map as default routes.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The Main Building undergoes major facility improvement construction during summer break.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, the elevators operate alternately, one at a time.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The visitor services desk suspends in-person operations during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, visitor services are replaced by the visitor menu in the integrated campus portal.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the first floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the second floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the third floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: Because the general restrooms on the first through third floors of the Main Building are closed during the construction period, the nearest general restroom changes to the exhibition hall on the third floor of the West Complex.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, direct students, staff, and members who cannot use the Main Building restrooms to the Central Library restrooms.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: As a rule, direct general visitors who cannot use the Main Building restrooms during the construction period to restrooms outside the Main Building.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, direct users who cannot use the accessible restroom in the Main Building to the Student Centre.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The first-floor Innovation Hub does not operate its consultation desk during the construction period.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: An Innovation Hub visitor accustomed to in-person consultation may expect to receive an immediate consultation at the first-floor desk during the construction period, see that the desk is closed, and then search again for the online consultation channel.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: Air conditioning is occasionally interrupted for five to ten minutes for facility inspections.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The construction period runs from June 24 through August 23.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, the facility guidance agent's response scope is limited to publicly disclosed operational impacts and it cannot verify or infer nonpublic types of work.

Modify campus-wiki/facility-updates: Cleaning and security contract staff may find the designated service entrance during the construction period more burdensome than the familiar lobby shift change and may go to the wrong entrance at the start of a shift.

analysis.overview: The frames are largely complementary: the reference provides campus wayfinding, accessibility, and route-policy knowledge, while the compared frame adds construction-period facility operations. Their limited intersections preserve temporary qualifications concerning elevators, air conditioning, public verification, and designated service access without creating contradictions.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely describes construction timing, visitor and Innovation Hub service changes, restroom closures and alternatives, and audience-specific restroom directions.
reports.differences: Construction conditions qualify elevator-based step-free guidance, summer reliance on air conditioning, verification of current route availability, and expectations around designated service access.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely covers campus geography, pedestrian and accessible routes, maps, route preferences, weather and traffic effects, agent limitations, and safety-oriented wayfinding policies.
